rejected_rule.statement: An affidavit of a deceased person can be used in a trial for its truth under Section 32(3) of the Evidence Ordinance if the statement is against the proprietary interest of the person making it.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: Section 32 of the Evidence Ordinance admits statements, written or verbal, of relevant facts, and made by persons who are dead. Section 32(3) makes statements of a deceased person relevant in a trial if, 1. it is a statement against the pecuniary or proprietary interest of the person making it; or 2. it is a statement which, if true, would expose him or would have exposed him to a criminal prosecution or to a suit for damages.
